headline: Shakira and Burna Boy headline 2026 World Cup opening ceremony in Mexico
summary: The 48-team tournament kicks off in Mexico, the US, and Canada with a star-studded show at the Estadio Azteca.
details: Colombian star Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy performed the official tournament song 'Dai Dai' at the Estadio Azteca on Thursday, sparking roars from the crowd.
The opening ceremony featured dancers and fireworks in the historic 80,000-capacity stadium, which has been renovated for the 2026 tournament.
This expanded 48-team tournament is being co-hosted by Mexico, the United States, and Canada, and will feature 104 games total.
The competition will culminate in the final match on July 19 in New Jersey.
While the stadium was festive, chaos erupted in Mexico City's Zocala plaza, where thousands of fans pushed and shoved to enter the official fan zone.
Access to the fan zone was hampered by metal barriers erected to prevent protesting teachers from reaching the area.
Some fans expressed frustration over the organization, with some hurling insults and water bottles at police as the site reached full capacity.
President Claudia Sheinbaum's attendance at the fan zone was cast in doubt due to the ongoing protests by teachers demanding pay rises.
caption:
Shakira and Burna Boy light up the Estadio Azteca! 🎤 The 2026 World Cup has officially begun.

Colombian star Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy performed the official tournament song 'Dai Dai' at the Estadio Azteca on Thursday, sparking roars from the crowd.

The opening ceremony featured dancers and fireworks in the historic 80,000-capacity stadium, which has been renovated for the 2026 tournament.

This expanded 48-team tournament is being co-hosted by Mexico, the United States, and Canada, and will feature 104 games total.

The competition will culminate in the final match on July 19 in New Jersey.

While the stadium was festive, chaos erupted in Mexico City's Zocala plaza, where thousands of fans pushed and shoved to enter the official fan zone.

Access to the fan zone was hampered by metal barriers erected to prevent protesting teachers from reaching the area.

Some fans expressed frustration over the organization, with some hurling insults and water bottles at police as the site reached full capacity.

President Claudia Sheinbaum's attendance at the fan zone was cast in doubt due to the ongoing protests by teachers demanding pay rises.
